_comment: __text baseline for the binary-size CI gate (see check_gate.py and .github/workflows/binary_size.yml). Measured osx-arm64, 2026-08-05. Regenerate after an intentional size change with: pixi run -e dev python3 benchmarks/binary_size/check_gate.py --update Last raised 2026-08-05 by M1.0, which widened comparison dispatch from NumericType to PrimitiveType: query_streaming +0.512%, query_join +1.154%. That is the cost of emitting comparison leaves for temporal, interval and decimal -- i.e. of supporting those dtypes at all -- and it buys row-group pruning on date and decimal predicates, which ClickBench needs. Lowered dramatically 2026-08-05 by Q4.7: hashing decoded dictionary keys via `cast`, which made all of `kernels.cast` reachable from every binary that hashes. Decoding by `take` instead removed ~2.4 MB from each -- query_join -63.5%, agg_fused -64.6%, agg -55.3%. Reset 2026-08-17 on the post-fix tree, and the history matters because the gate was red by 42-96% at the time, not by the +0.449% the backlog recorded. Investigating before resetting attributed nearly all of it to one commit: f5226d5 ("migrate closures to the unified value-taking form") added +739,316 bytes (+54.8%) to query_streaming_agg_fused, while its own commit message and CHANGELOG entry claimed "Binary size max +0.36%". A single-variable A/B settles it -- f5226d5 and its parent 5435f59 build with the identical pinned toolchain and measure 2,089,084 vs 1,349,768. The Mojo 1.1 / MAX 26.6 upgrade accounted for only +0.39%, and GPU gating was intact (-D MARROW_GPU=true still costs +308,008, and no device symbols reach a default build). The cause was the interposed `narrow` closure layer in the shared variant_dispatch helper, whose DynArray-returning instantiations were 55.9% of __text; removing it recovered 662,740 bytes (89.6%) and roughly halved cold build times. Old -> new here: query_streaming 1,332,456 -> 1,484,652 (+11.4%), query_join 1,410,788 -> 1,507,836 (+6.9%), query_streaming_agg_fused 1,338,468 -> 1,417,476 (+5.9%), query_streaming_agg 1,858,644 -> 1,932,404 (+4.0%). That residue is ~600 commits of legitimate work plus V0's measured +0.136% (ListScalar carrying its own dtype, so a map element reports map<...> rather than list<struct<...>>). threshold_pct stays 0.5 -- it is what caught this, and it is not raised. The real lesson is not the reset: a +55% regression survived ten commits because this gate is not in CI and CI has not run since 2026-05-11 (backlog section 2). Added query_dynvalue 2026-08-18 (S4/A1): the four gates above link *zero* symbols from marrow.kernels.cast -- checked with `nm -C` on all eleven benchmark binaries -- so the entire cast family was ungated, and a change that added +435,072 bytes (+7.09%) to query_dynvalue measured 0.00% on every gate the CI actually watches. query_dynvalue links 693 cast symbols (query_runtime and query_sort also link the ladder and are still ungated; one gate was judged enough signal for the cost of the extra sweep time). Its baseline is recorded at 4,871,156, which is 1,268,480 bytes BELOW the 6,139,636 measured at 8cc9723: splitting DecimalCast's single _convert[FromN, ToN] -- monomorphized over the full decimal-union-numeric cross product on both sides -- into five per-conversion kernels narrowed each one's dispatch to the families it can actually see. The lesson is the gate gap, not the win: 1,476 bytes of added source cost 371,584 bytes of __text through that cross product, a 250x multiplier that nothing would have reported.
